hadith:
Wedlock, Marriage (Nikaah) - Narrated Sahl:

When Abu Usaid As-Sa`idi got married, he invited the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions. None prepared the food for them and brought it to them but his wife. She soaked some dates in water in a stone pot overnight, and when the Prophet (ﷺ) had finished his food, she provided him with that drink (of soaked dates).
message: Wealth and worldly possessions are temporary and will not save us on the Day of Judgment, as Allah reminds us in Surah Al-Masad. Instead, true benefit comes from sincere actions and serving others with kindness—like the wife in the hadith who humbly prepared food for the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions. Let us trust in Al-Jabbaar, the Compeller and Restorer, who alone holds the power to rectify our affairs and guide us toward what truly matters.
name:
Al Jabbaar - الْجَبَّارُ - The Compeller

Al Jabbaar, meaning 'The Compeller' or 'The Restorer', reflects Allah's supreme ability to enforce His will upon creation. It emphasizes His power to rectify and restore all that is broken or unjust. This name highlights Allah's dominion over the universe, ensuring that justice and order prevail according to His divine plan.
verse:
Al-Masad - The Palm Fiber - 111:2

Neither his wealth nor ˹worldly˺ gains will benefit him.
